source.title: Fortuitous Forgetting in Connectionist Networks
source.authors: Hattie Zhou; Ankit Vani; H. Larochelle; Aaron C. Courville

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether iterative forgetting and retraining affect generalization, using test accuracy comparisons. It does not test the specific mechanisms or measurements named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports training accuracy after forgetting and test accuracy after iterative retraining. Its random or mislabeled-example results concern training accuracy after weight perturbation, not held-out generalization; cited findings from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study tests selective weight forgetting and retraining, which none of V1–V8 names. Random-label experiments measure training accuracy after perturbation, without the held-out natural-versus-random-label comparison required by V1. Weight perturbation is neither the magnitude-aware sharpness comparison in V7 nor removal of memorized training examples in V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose that selective forgetting preserves useful information and that relearning strengthens features useful across changing initial conditions. LLF improves several small-data image benchmarks and Tiny-ImageNet, but not the tested CIFAR settings. The proposed general mechanism remains a hypothesis supported by their analyses.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses iterative weight perturbation and retraining, including later-layer forgetting, rather than the interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported LLF advantage depends on the dataset and model setting: the authors report no improvement on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, while Tiny-ImageNet shows a gain.

fits_no_version.finding: LLF improves accuracy over equal-computation continued training on the five small image datasets, but does not improve the reported CIFAR settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterative later-layer reinitialization and retraining can improve image-classification accuracy, with benefits depending on the dataset and training setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Partial weight perturbations disproportionately reduce training accuracy on difficult or randomly labeled examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some weight perturbations preferentially disrupt fitted difficult or mislabeled examples relative to easy or correctly labeled examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Partial balanced forgetting improves emergent-language topographic similarity relative to receiver resetting or no resetting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting and retraining both communicating agents can increase emergent-language compositionality.

record.problems: The CIFAR extension reports only small or negative differences; Table A8 does not state uncertainty. Table 1 reports best validation-selected hyperparameter settings. Some other results are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only results on Flower test accuracy for KE, LLF, reversed LLF and layer-freezing analyses (Figure 3) were not extracted because values are not stated numerically. Figure-only results on language topographic similarity (Figure 4) concern compositionality rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: The paired demonstration of random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout ablations and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Removing high-memorization training examples versus equally many random examples and measuring accuracy after retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All eight rows correctly have no version links. Their reported performance differences concern a separate intervention, so they warrant no verdict on V1–V8. The discussion of memorization's contribution to generalization cites Feldman and Zhang rather than testing example removal.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural and random labels.
Network width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effect of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting held-out accuracy.
